statement: A DevOps-savvy operator can stand up a multi-node Lagrange cluster — locally via 'docker compose up' and on Kubernetes via the charts/lagrange Helm chart (StatefulSet, per-pod stable NODE_ID, PVC-backed Raft/SQLite, probes, headless+sql+admin services) — from a published multi-arch ghcr.io image, and reach a working psql SQL round-trip by following getting-started-compose.md or getting-started-kubernetes.md, within ~30 minutes (Phase 0.5 exit criterion); the chart render-gate runs in test:ci.

doneWhenSealed.closure: operator-attested against the W0-W5 acceptance checklist (artifact-bound, each verifiable by a script/CI job, not a statistical bar); the oracle probe is the machine liveness signal and is set to done only when every workstream artifact is green (metric=0). Mirrors the operator-attested closure convention used by rolling-restart quests.
doneWhenSealed.onboardingModel: Lagrange is a distributed data+service platform; the SQL/pgsql endpoint is just one managed service it runs. W0 proved (2026-06-28) a bare SINGLE seed opens 8080/8081/8082 but NOT 5432. POST-REVIEW CORRECTION: pgsql is NOT 'stopped' — its definition ships status='active', replica_count=3 (meta-service-factory.js:85-102, wasm-service-models.js:156-173); 5432 is closed because no REPLICA was PLACED, and status is not the lever that places it (placement is driven by the rebalancer + RuntimeServiceHandler + pgwire-runtime-module.start). The real precondition on a small cluster is unpinned (W0b). Onboarding teaches the platform model; the exact psql step depends on the Key open decision (auto-start on >=3 nodes vs ship-not-started + explicit start).
doneWhenSealed.keyOpenDecision: D1 auto-start (no product change; psql comes up on a healthy >=3-node cluster; teach service mgmt via hello-world deploy) vs D2 ship-not-started (change the built-in pgsql definition to not-started + implement a real server-side 'service start' action; matches the 'start the SQL service' narrative). Decide after W0b. See solve/epics/lagrange-devops-onboarding.md 'Key open decision'.
criteria: W0 (RESOLVED 2026-06-28): a bare single seed does NOT open 5432; pgwire listener opens only when a runtime-service replica is PLACED (src/runtime/pgwire-cutover-guard.js, pgwire-runtime-module.js:256-270). NOT a status flag — definition ships active+replica_count=3.

W0b (BLOCKER): pin why the PG-wire replica is not placed on a 1-node cluster and whether a healthy 3-node cluster places it automatically; document the minimal precondition for 5432 to open (rebalancer critical-topology path unified-rebalancer-critical-topology-methods.js:428-508; safety gate pgwire-startup-safety-gate.js:118-136). Resolves the Key open decision and whether WS-API 'start' is needed.

WS-API: a SQL-free 'lagrange service list/status/scale/deploy' verb surface (read verbs join service_definitions x service_endpoints/services for placed/healthy state; scale/deploy reuse meta-command-handlers.js builders); under decision D2 it ALSO includes server-side 'start'/'stop' actions (no SQL builder exists; status is not the lever; stop must scale-to-0/REMOVE, not flip status). No flags, no dead knobs. Admin-WS query envelope + SQL templates documented as the automation surface. (Auth is a SEPARATE follow-on quest; quickstart is localhost-only with a trusted-boundary warning.)

WS-HELLO: a minimal hello-world service + manifest in examples/ (supplying handlerFunctionId) deploys via WS-API on a >=3-node cluster (odd, >=3 replica floor); following the doc, the operator deploys it and reaches its endpoint.
W1: a tagged build publishes multi-arch (linux/amd64+arm64) ghcr.io//lagrange: and :latest; a CI job pulls it and 'docker run --rm --version' prints the version and '--dry-run' exits clean.

W2: 'docker compose up -d' forms a converged >=3-node cluster (all /readyz return 200); psql round-trip (CREATE TABLE / INSERT / SELECT) succeeds — automatically (D1) or after 'lagrange service start sys-postgres-wire' (D2), with no raw SQL typed; after 'docker compose restart' data and NODE_IDs are unchanged and the cluster re-converges. Verified by scripts/verify-compose-quickstart.sh.

W3: 'helm lint' is clean and 'helm template' for default + custom (replicas=5, custom storageClassName, non-root securityContext) renders the three probes on 8080, a headless service (clusterIP: None), volumeClaimTemplates mounted at /data, and lagrange-sql(5432)/lagrange-admin(8081) services. Gated by scripts/check-lagrange-chart.js, wired into test:ci.

W4: on kind, 'helm install' (>=3 replicas) brings all PVCs to Bound and all pods to passing /startupz+/readyz; lagrange-0 is the seed (no SEED_NODE_ADDRESS) and others joined; 'kubectl port-forward svc/lagrange-sql 5432' + psql round-trip succeeds; 'kubectl delete pod lagrange-1' rebinds the same PVC with the same NODE_ID and rejoins with data intact. Verified by scripts/verify-chart-on-kind.sh.

W5: docs/getting-started-compose.md and docs/getting-started-kubernetes.md exist; their command blocks ARE the W2/W4 verify scripts (narrated), walking the onboarding model end to end (cluster up -> list services -> reach psql -> deploy hello-world -> reach its endpoint), satisfying the Phase 0.5 exit criterion.

constraints.statement: Resolve W0 (psql/pgwire availability) before authoring any doc or acceptance that assumes 'connect with psql' works — pgwire is a gated runtime service whose failure is isolated, so a node can report bootstrap-complete with no 5432 listener (src/bootstrap/bootstrap-service-control-plane-runtime-methods.js:121-143).

Do not expose chart/compose values that map to ignored config: NODE_WS_PORT is not in ENV_MAPPINGS and admin port 8081 is hardcoded (src/admin/admin-websocket-api-base.js:153). Document these as known constraints; do not add knobs that silently do nothing.

Seed/join env wiring (NODE_ID, NODE_ADDRESS, SEED_NODE_ADDRESS, DATA_DIR, TRANSPORT_WS_HOST, advertised WS) must match the proven harness wiring in test/distributed/harness/cluster-class-lifecycle-base.js:270-319; NODE_ID must be stable per replica (unset => new uuidv4 each boot).
If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.
